Part I — Knowledge Base (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 126, English)
Ashaeiynn: Mool Tattva — Mantra Japa vs. Dhyana (Meditation), and Why This Teaching Prioritizes Mantra

This session opens with a fr esh framing (" जो आशय से जुड़े हैं... मैं समझता हूं िक मूल तत्व सेशन हमारे और आपके मुलाकात का एक सबसे अहम तत्व है") marking it as a new , distinct "Mool T attva" (foundational) Sunday-style session, held even without a specific pr e-planned topic. The session opens with light, personal banter with the live gr oup, moves thr ough brief individual guidance and general community r emarks, and continues into an extended, audience-interactive doctrinal teaching on the differ ence between mantra japa (mantra r epetition) and dhyana (meditation). A continuation piece with no fr esh opening of its own — beginning dir ectly with an explanation of "adhishthatri devata" (personal pr esiding deities) that a participant had asked about earlier in the same live session — is mer ged in her e as Part H, along with a teaching on pitru (ancestral spirits) and the start of an individual participant checking/r oll-call segment. Because this session includes a substantial amount of genuine, quotable live back-andforth with named participants (playful banter , a gr oup guessing exer cise, and light rumor -addr essing humor), a separate Hinglish curated-conversation document is included alongside this Knowledge Base and the accompanying Q&A document. Segments of individual personal guidance to named participants ar e generalized her e, consistent with this pr oject's standing privacy practice for live personal spiritual "checking"; a devotional anecdote r eferencing a r eal, deceased public figur e (Part H) is recor ded strictly as Bhaiya's own personal, illustrative account, not a claim this document tr eats as verified.
Part A — Framing: Why Mool Tattva Sessions Matter

1. The value Bhaiya places on this session format: He describes Mool Tattva sessions as the most important element of his and the community's ongoing relationship, since it is a format where he gets to know participants more closely and vice versa, and where — per this teaching — the guru "takes shape" within that mutual familiarity , producing significant learning.

2. Playful framing of how a Sunday evening should be spent: Bhaiya jokes that attending is a better use of a Sunday evening than watching Netflix or Prime, leading to a lighthearted exchange with participants (recorded in the accompanying Hinglish curated document) in which he is teasingly called the group's "Netflix."

3. A teaching about what makes this path distinctive, per Bhaiya: He states that in physical, mental, or emotional strength, far more accomplished people exist elsewhere in the world; what this path specifically cultivates, in his framing, is "astral strength" — attained through meditative/mantra practice that produces alignment and focus.
Part B — Individual Guidance (Generalized)

1. Guidance offer ed to a participant whose r ecent kul devta (ancestral deity) havan was specifically drishti-r elated: Bhaiya told him his perceptive abilities/ener gies would grow as a result, and cautioned that this might feel overwhelming — he might begin perceiving a great deal about many things, both favorable and unfavorable — since the participant had specifically requested acceleration ("push"). Bhaiya advised him to stay steady , avoid becoming emotionally attached to whatever he

perceives, never stop his japa regardless of what he perceives, and to deliberately ignore any perceived "truth" that seems to be pulling him away from his practice or his guru — explaining that as one begins to understand deep concepts (the mechanics of creation, for instance), doubt in the guiding powers can creep in, and that he should consult his assigned mentor if he feels unsettled by anything he perceives.
Part C — Being "W atched," and Why High-Caliber Devotees Aren't Named Publicly

1. Bhaiya's account of ongoing, informal checking: He states that devotees who take their practice seriously are personally checked by him every two to three days even without this being announced publicly , and that dedicated practitioners "stand out" to him without needing to say anything.

2. Why accomplished devotees ar e deliberately not named publicly , per this teaching: Bhaiya explains that naming or publicly highlighting a specific devotee tends to draw unwanted attention — other participants approaching them with questions, building myths around them, or pressuring them — and that public praise can also risk inflating a devotee's own ego ("I am ahead of everyone"), which this teaching considers spiritually undesirable; he states he tries to protect devotees from both ef fects by not naming them.

3. On "character" as a criterion: Bhaiya states a devotee's outward character/personality is not, per this teaching, a reliable indicator of devotion, since it constantly changes over time; the criteria he uses instead are adherence to the guru's rules and consistent practice of the prescribed japa.
Part D — On Very High Japa Counts and Self-Doubt

1. Reassurance for a devotee who feels they have "r eceived nothing" despite an extr emely large volume of japa (e.g., "2 cror e"/20 million r epetitions): Per this teaching, simply being able to sustain that volume of japa is itself only possible because of an already-present underlying spiritual support or power — illustrated with an analogy to a horse wearing blinders (staying focused forward rather than looking side to side, since looking away causes it to stop) — and Bhaiya states plainly that such a devotee already has significant spiritual power , just not yet recognizing it, cautioning against unquestioning "blind faith" that prevents someone from recognizing power they already possess.

2. A contrasting caution: Bhaiya states that a person who never actually practices japa, and who only makes demands ("give me this, give me that"), cannot be helped by the guru's grace even if the guide wished to help them — framing consistent personal practice, not mere requests, as the necessary condition for any of this teaching's claimed benefits.
Part E — Community Attendance, Public Criticism, and an Upcoming "Pathshala" (School)

1. On havan attendance and mixed motives, per this teaching: Bhaiya describes the range of personal concerns people bring to havan (negativity , ancestral/pitru issues, physical or financial problems) and says he finds it endearing that, of a typical lar ge gathering (200+ people), more than 80% do sincere japa despite acknowledging their own self-interested motives — framing self-interested motivation as ordinary and acceptable, while stating what he personally values is the devotional process itself, which he compares to how Hanuman ji Maharaj is traditionally described as having practiced devotion.

2. Bhaiya's personal, subjective account of his own past r elationship with mainstr eam science: He states that he personally valued science highly before living close to his guru, but that since then he has come to see mainstream science as, in his own words, comparatively a "facade" or "pretense" relative to his personal spiritual path — of fered explicitly as his own subjective viewpoint and personal history , not a claim this document treats as an objective statement about science.

3. Addressing public rumors and criticism, with humor: Bhaiya jokes about circulating claims that the group's extensive havan practice contributes to climate change, and about a lighthearted family exchange in which a recent geopolitical ceasefire was jokingly attributed to his influence — treating both as examples of exaggerated rumor and "marketing" by unnamed others. Separately , and as devotional history rather than a claim this document verifies, he states that historically significant royalsponsored havans (including one attributed to Ram) were powerful enough that "even devatas set down their weapons," contrasting this with what he describes as the comparatively small scale of Ashaeiynn's own current havan practice.

4. Announcement of "Ashaeiynn Pathshala" (school): Educational videos and articles are described as being prepared for release via YouT ube and syncing into the app, intended to make foundational teaching accessible to devotees who cannot attend live sessions regularly .
Part F — Brief Logistics Q&A
1. Japa during a woman's monthly cycle after Gyaan Tattva sadhna: Permitted, provided the practitioner has also completed aura "shielding"; without shielding, japa should be paused during the cycle.

2. A question about visiting Radha Rani in meditation/travel practice: Bhaiya states this is possible within this practice, identifying Radha Rani with Sita Mata per this teaching, and states he has personally "seen" this himself.

3. Prerequisite for aura shielding: Any aura-shielding must first be authorized by the guru through the participant's assigned mentor; participants without that authorization yet are told to pray daily and do two hours of daily japa, which is described as making authorization more likely to be granted.

4. A planned in-app featur e: A savings/fund-storage option is described as being planned within the app, to let devotees contribute toward donations gradually rather than needing to give a lar ge amount at once.
Part G — Doctrine: The Difference Between Mantra Japa and Dhyana (Meditation)

1. The session's central question, posed to the gr oup: Why does this teaching emphasize mantra japa specifically , rather than meditation/dhyana alone? Bhaiya invites numerous participants to answer before of fering his own extended explanation (the group's varied answers are recorded in the accompanying Hinglish curated document).

2. Definition of dhyana (meditation), per this teaching: Continuous focus on any single object, image, mantra, or concept — described with the analogy of a magnifying glass: whatever one focuses on through meditation becomes "magnified"/intensified and expanded.

3. The central doctrinal claim distinguishing meditation fr om mantra japa: Meditation is described as working by awakening and expanding the practitioner's own inner "atma tattva" (self/soul element) — the practitioner projects their own inner ener gy outward, making them self-suf ficient but also solely responsible for , and limited to, whatever their own atma tattva can accomplish. Per this teaching's own framework, every devotional image or murti that has ever seemed to "come alive" through meditation is explained as a reflection of the practitioner's or saint's own awakened atma tattva projected outward, not literally an independent external force acting on its own initiative.

4. The central doctrinal claim about mantra japa, by contrast: Mantra japa is described as a mechanism for directing and drawing on external, otherworldly cooperation — engaging beings and entities across the "sookshm jagat" (subtle world) to act on the practitioner's behalf, rather than relying solely on self-generated inner ener gy . Per this teaching's own cosmology , a mantra properly received from a guru and consistently practiced is said to be able to bind or compel cooperation from a wide range of subtle-world entities (a named list of traditional spirit/entity categories is given, along with the claim that, per this teaching, sustained devotion can ultimately bind even deities through vows and devotional bonds). This document records this
strictly as this teaching's own devotional/cosmological framework, not as a claim this document treats as objectively verified fact — see the Bot Response Guidelines regarding this content.

5. Bhaiya's stated personal r easoning for preferring mantra japa over self-reliant meditation: He describes meditationbased self-reliance ("main tattva," a self/individual-centered approach) as placing the full burden of validating one's own spiritual progress — including against outside scrutiny or skepticism — on the individual practitioner , which he personally finds psychologically taxing in a socially comparison-driven context. By contrast, he describes mantra japa as placing that responsibility on the guru/lineage rather than the individual, which he states he personally finds more sustainable and less prone to inflating personal ego, referencing a traditional couplet attributed to Tulsidas about placing complete trust in one's mantra. This is of fered as Bhaiya's own devotional and pedagogical preference for this teaching's community , not a claim that other spiritual approaches are invalid.

6. Acknowledgment of other appr oaches: Bhaiya acknowledges that other well-known contemporary spiritual movements and teachers have chosen to emphasize a self/individual-centered ("main tattva") approach instead, framing this as a legitimate but dif ferent choice suited to a more individualistic cultural moment, rather than declaring that approach false — while restating his own personal and pedagogical preference for the guru-mantra approach taught within Ashaeiynn.

7. A closing devotional teaching using traditional couplets: A couplet attributed to Tulsidas (" मंत्र जाप कर दृढ़ िवश्वासा, पंचम भजन सो वेद प�काशा") and one attributed to Kabir are used to illustrate complete surrender of personal ego/ownership (" मैं नहीं, मेरा नहीं" — "not I, not mine") to the guru and mantra, rather than relying on self-directed spiritual ef fort.

8. A large numeric devotional claim (r ecorded strictly as devotional teaching, not a literal or verifiable guarantee): Per this teaching, sustained recitation of a single guru-given mantra to "14 crore" (140 million) repetitions is described as guaranteeing that even a person carrying every conceivable spiritual af fliction would receive direct, physical darshan of Sitaram — framed explicitly as a devotional promise tied to unwavering persistence in mantra japa specifically , not meditation. See the Bot Response Guidelines regarding this claim.

9. Practical pr ocess guidance for newer practitioners: Initial practice should be done seated (not while walking or multitasking) until a described set of "12 spheres"/"quantum points" are filled, per this teaching; only after the guru grants permission for a later stage does continuous, ambient japa throughout daily activity become appropriate.

10. Closing note on humility: Participants who benefit from these communal ener gies/powers are told a degree of humility and freedom from ego/arrogance is expected, since, per this teaching, planetary/astrological influences are described as attaching specifically to unresolved ego-driven tendencies (desire, anger , greed, pride, attachment, envy) — practicing without arrogance is framed as reducing exposure to these influences.
Part H — The Four Body-Governing Deities, and a Teaching on Pitru (Ancestral Spirits)

1. The four personal "adhishthatri" (pr esiding) deities, per this teaching: Bhaiya describes four deities said to govern distinct elements of every person's body and subtle constitution. The first, the adhishthatri devata proper , is described as governing the "space element" — the channel through which all of a person's past-life powers and subtle bodies are said to arrive; per this teaching, appeasing this deity is described as a way to access many of those latent powers at once.

2. The second deity: governing blood: Described as controlling blood flow and blood pressure throughout the body; per this teaching, "medical drishti" (the ability to perceive bodily conditions) begins with the ability to see blood flow , and most disease is attributed, per this teaching, to disruptions in blood flow specifically . This document also records, as a doctrinal aside describing a dif ferent school of thought (not this teaching's own core practice), that some practitioners who follow this deity's teachings hold that all bodily elements — including veerya (reproductive/vital ener gy) — should be regularly "renewed" through natural change rather than retained, drawing an analogy to cell regeneration and advocating for regular physical intimacy on that basis; this is recorded strictly as a doctrinal contrast Bhaiya describes (attributed to practitioners of Ayurveda's
vata-pitta-kapha framework and Patanjali's yoga sutras), not as this teaching's own prescription — see the Bot Response Guidelines.

3. The third deity: governing vayu (air/br eath): Described as controlling the body's breath pressure and, per this teaching, personal power broadly; illustrated with the traditional description of Hanuman ji Maharaj and Bhima as "vayu putras" (sons of the wind) known for their strength. Two breath categories are described (urdhvagami, upward-moving, said to increase the rajas/passionate element; and dir ghagami, long/deep breath, said to increase both sattvic and tamasic elements); per this teaching, greater breath capacity corresponds to greater personal ener gy , illustrated with the physiological claim that oxygen (not food directly) is the proximate source of bodily ener gy , food's role being to supply the ener gy needed to process oxygen.

4. The traditional illustrative story of Hanuman ji Maharaj and the vayu/earth elements, per this teaching: Hanuman ji is described as having been born with his available ener gy concentrated in the lower body; concerned saints and his mother , Mata Anjana, are said to have had this ener gy deliberately bound through spiritual means, leaving him comparatively powerless, until — per this account — he undertook knowledge, meditation (dhyana), and sadhna to draw that ener gy upward, becoming, per this teaching, "master of masters." Mata Anjana is described as having also secretly taught him that the vayu (air) element and prithvi/earth element are mutually repelling — meaning a person strong in one is typically not "attractive" or charismatic in the other — and that this is why Hanuman ji Maharaj, per this retelling, deliberately sought Sita Mata's blessing and touch (rather than going first to Ram) specifically to gain the "earth element" attractiveness/grace that would complete his vayu-based power , illustrated with the devotional framing that Hanuman ji and Ram together "complete the cycle" of these two elements.

5. The fourth deity: governing the earth element: Described visually , per this teaching, as stone-like, lar gely motionless beings; said to govern a person's "magnetic force" — their ability to attract or repel others — independent of a person's other strengths (e.g., a very intelligent or physically powerful person may still lack this attractiveness if this element is weak in them).

6. Kul devta's place r elative to these four: Per this teaching, kul devta (family/ancestral deities) are described as roughly "1 1 levels above" these four personal body-governing deities, described metaphorically as many generations senior to them.

7. A closing note on devotional traditions built ar ound these elements: Bhaiya states that research and devotional practice have historically formed around each of these four elements separately , each producing its own culture and tradition ("cult"), and states that each such tradition is valid within its own context ("har cult apni jagah sahi hai") — of fered as his own view , with a joking aside not to be taken literally that one should never speak against any such tradition.
Part I — A Teaching on Pitru (Ancestral Spirits), and the Start of an Individual Checking Session

1. Individual guidance (generalized) to a participant experiencing a sudden headache: After she prayed against negative ancestral influence af fecting her , Bhaiya attributed her headache to her own pitru (ancestral spirits) reacting to that prayer , describing this as evidence the prayer had taken ef fect and that their influence would diminish "day by day" as she continues havan and practice, framing the immediate discomfort as a positive sign rather than cause for alarm.

2. Whose pitru ar e typically pr esent, per this teaching: Ancestral spirits are usually from the father's side, unless the mother's kul devta has been specifically established in the home or the family follows the mother's kul devta line, in which case maternal ancestral spirits may also be present.

3. General teaching on pitru attachment, per this teaching: Bhaiya describes pitru as reluctant to "let go" of living descendants, wanting the recognition and connection ("hak," a claim/right) that blood relation gives them, and states that clearing this attachment is important because it allows other , non-ancestral spiritual connections and relationships ("purv janam ki shakti," powers/relationships from past lives) to reach the practitioner more fully — illustrated with the claim that people with very few close relationships or supportive people around them often have unusually strong, binding pitru attachment, while those who clear it experience a marked increase in supportive relationships and "manifestation."

4. A cautionary folk anecdote about a deceased guru's spirit (r ecorded per this project's standing "extract everything" practice, with the Bot Response Guidelines flagging appr opriate caution): Bhaiya describes, without naming anyone, a claimed case in which a deceased guru's spirit is said to have gone on to disturb his own disciple's household in a sexually inappropriate way — of fered as an extreme illustration that not all lingering spirits, even those of respected figures, are benevolent, and that unresolved attachment after death can take troubling forms.

5. A devotional anecdote r eferencing a r eal, deceased public figur e: Bhaiya recounts a personal claim of having perceived, during meditation, the ancestral spirits (pitru) of the late Indian finance minister Arun Jaitley at the time of his passing, describing what he depicts as an unusually lar ge number of devoted, loving people ("apne log") supporting him to the end — of fered as Bhaiya's own personal, illustrative anecdote about the general principle that well-loved people are surrounded by many supportive relationships, not a claim this document treats as verified information about Arun Jaitley specifically . See the Bot Response Guidelines.

6. A collective "mantra shakti" sankalp (vow) mentioned for a named gr oup of participants: Bhaiya states he has taken a mantra shakti sankalp on behalf of a specific list of named devotees; no further personal or diagnostic detail about them is given in this transcript.

7. The start of an individual participant checking/r oll-call segment: Following the general teaching, Bhaiya begins calling participants in sequence for individual checking; this transcript captures only the beginning of the roll call (the sequence of names to be checked) and not yet the checking content itself, which appears to continue in a subsequent recording.
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

The mantra-vs-meditation doctrine in Part G (including the claim that mantra can bind or compel cooperation fr om subtle-world entities, up to and including deities) is r ecorded strictly as this teaching's own devotional/cosmological framework , not independently verifiable fact, and must never be presented as a literal claim that mantra can compel real people or supernatural entities to act. The "14 cr or e japa guarantees dir ect darshan" claim (point 25) is devotional teaching, not a literal or verifiable timeline or guarantee — never present it to a real user as a promise the bot can validate. Part B's individual guidance to a named participant has been generalized rather than attributed by name , consistent with this project's standing privacy practice for live personal spiritual "checking." Bhaiya's r emarks about mainstr eam science (point 1 1) ar e recorded as his own personal, subjective viewpoint and history , not an objective claim about science this document endorses. Part B (point 29) describes a differ ent school of thought's view that veerya should be r egularly "discarded" via physical intimacy — this is r ecorded as a doctrinal contrast Bhaiya describes, NOT this teaching's own pr escription , and must never be presented as medical or relationship advice. The Arun Jaitley anecdote (point 39) and the deceased-guru-spirit anecdote (point 38) ar e Bhaiya's own personal, illustrative, devotional accounts — never present either as verified fact , and never use the deceased-guru anecdote as a template to make claims about any real, identifiable religious figure. Part I's individual guidance and r oll-call segment involve r eal named participants and have been generalized or left unelaborated rather than attributing personal diagnostic content by name, consistent with this project's standing privacy practice. This session includes a separate Hinglish curated-conversation document (Part III of the combined PDF), reflecting the genuine, quotable live banter and audience interaction in this session, alongside this Knowledge Base and the accompanying Q&A document. Part II — Q&A Pairs (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Q&A Pairs (Session 126, English)
Ashaeiynn: Mool Tattva — Mantra Japa vs. Dhyana (Meditation), and Why This Teaching Prioritizes Mantra

Q1. Why does Bhaiya say Mool Tattva sessions matter so much? A1. He describes them as the most important element of his relationship with the community — a format where he gets to know participants closely and, per this teaching, where the guru "takes shape" in that mutual familiarity .

Q2. What guidance was given to a participant whose r ecent kul devta havan was drishti-r elated? A2. He was told his perceptive abilities would grow , possibly overwhelmingly , and was advised to stay steady , avoid emotional attachment to what he perceives, never stop his japa, ignore any perceived "truth" pulling him from his practice, and consult his mentor if unsettled.

Q3. Why does Bhaiya avoid publicly naming high-caliber devotees? A3. He states public naming draws unwanted attention, mythmaking, and pressure from other participants, and can also risk inflating the named devotee's own ego — both ef fects he tries to avoid by not naming them.

Q4. What criteria does this teaching use to judge a devotee, according to Bhaiya, instead of outward "character"? A4. Adherence to the guru's rules and consistent practice of the prescribed japa — character is described as constantly changing and therefore unreliable as a criterion.

Q5. What r eassurance does Bhaiya offer someone who feels they've "r eceived nothing" despite an enormous volume of japa? A5. That simply being able to sustain that volume of japa is itself only possible with an already-present underlying spiritual power , illustrated with a horse-blinders analogy , and that such a devotee already has significant power , just not yet recognizing it.

Q6. What does Bhaiya say about people who only make demands without practicing japa? A6. That they cannot be helped by the guru's grace even if the guide wished to help them — consistent personal practice, not requests alone, is described as the necessary condition.

Q7. How does Bhaiya addr ess public criticism that the gr oup's havan practice harms the climate? A7. With humor , treating it as exaggerated rumor and "marketing" by others, while separately describing (as devotional history , not verified fact) that historically significant royal-sponsored havans were powerful enough that "devatas set down their weapons."

Q8. What is "Ashaeiynn Pathshala"? A8. An upcoming educational resource — videos and articles released via YouT ube and synced into the app — intended to make foundational teaching accessible to devotees who can't attend live sessions regularly .

Q9. Can a woman continue mantra japa during her monthly cycle after Gyaan Tattva sadhna? A9. Yes, provided she has also completed aura "shielding"; without shielding, japa should be paused during the cycle.

Q10. What is r equired befor e a participant can get aura shielding? A10. Authorization from the guru through the participant's assigned mentor; without it, participants are told to pray daily and do two hours of daily japa, which is said to make authorization more likely .

Q1 1. What is the central question Bhaiya poses in this session's main teaching? A1 1. Why does this teaching emphasize mantra japa specifically , rather than meditation/dhyana alone? He invites the group to answer before giving his own explanation.

Q12. How does this teaching define dhyana (meditation)? A12. Continuous focus on a single object, image, mantra, or concept — compared to a magnifying glass, intensifying and expanding whatever is focused on.

Q13. What is the central doctrinal claim about how meditation works, per this teaching? A13. Meditation awakens and projects the practitioner's own inner "atma tattva" (self/soul element) outward — making the practitioner self-suf ficient but also solely responsible for , and limited to, whatever their own atma tattva can accomplish; every devotional image that has seemed to "come alive" is explained, per this teaching, as a reflection of the practitioner's own awakened atma tattva.

Q14. What is the central doctrinal claim about how mantra japa works, per this teaching? A14. That it directs and draws on external, otherworldly cooperation from beings across the "sookshm jagat" (subtle world) to act on the practitioner's behalf, rather than relying solely on self-generated inner ener gy — described, per this teaching's own cosmology , as able to bind cooperation from a wide range of subtle-world entities, and, per this teaching, ultimately even deities through vows and devotional bonds.

Q15. Why does Bhaiya personally pr efer mantra japa over self-reliant meditation? A15. He describes meditation-based selfreliance as placing the full burden of validating one's own progress on the individual, which he finds psychologically taxing in a socially comparison-driven context, while mantra japa places that responsibility on the guru/lineage — which he finds more sustainable and less prone to inflating personal ego. This is of fered as his own devotional and pedagogical preference, not a claim that other approaches are invalid.

Q16. Does Bhaiya say other spiritual teachers who emphasize a self-center ed ("main tattva") appr oach ar e wrong? A16. No — he describes it as a legitimate but dif ferent choice suited to a more individualistic cultural moment, while restating his own preference for the guru-mantra approach.

Q17. What large numeric claim does Bhaiya make about sustained mantra japa? A17. That reciting a single guru-given mantra to "14 crore" (140 million) repetitions is described, per this teaching, as guaranteeing direct, physical darshan of Sitaram even for someone carrying every conceivable spiritual af fliction — of fered strictly as devotional teaching, not a literal or verifiable guarantee.

Q18. What pr ocess guidance is given to newer practitioners about how and wher e to practice? A18. Initial practice should be done seated, not while walking or multitasking, until a described set of "12 spheres"/"quantum points" are filled; only after the guru grants a later stage does continuous, ambient japa become appropriate.

Q19. What ar e the four "adhishthatri" (pr esiding) body-governing deities described in Part H? A19. A deity governing the "space element" (channel for past-life powers), a deity governing blood flow , a deity governing vayu/breath (linked to personal power), and a deity governing the "earth element" (linked to attractiveness/charisma) — with kul devta described as roughly 1 1 levels above these four .

Q20. What traditional story illustrates the vayu and earth elements, per this teaching? A20. The story of Hanuman ji Maharaj, whose ener gy was initially bound low in the body until meditation and sadhna raised it, making him powerful (vayu element); Mata Anjana is said to have secretly taught him that vayu and earth elements repel each other , so he sought Sita Mata's blessing specifically to gain the earth element's attractiveness to complete his power .

Q21. What does this teaching say usually determines whose pitru (ancestral spirits) ar e present ar ound a person? A21. Typically the father's side, unless the mother's kul devta has been specifically established in the home or the family follows the mother's line.

Q22. Why does this teaching say clearing pitru attachment matters? A22. Because pitru are described as reluctant to "let go" of descendants and can crowd out other supportive relationships and past-life connections; clearing this attachment is said to lead to a marked increase in supportive relationships and successful "manifestation."

Q23. What personal anecdote does Bhaiya shar e involving a r eal public figur e? A23. A claim of having perceived, during meditation, the ancestral spirits of the late Indian finance minister Arun Jaitley at the time of his passing, describing an unusually lar ge number of devoted people supporting him — of fered as Bhaiya's own personal, illustrative anecdote, not verified information about Arun Jaitley .
Bot Response Guidelines

1. Present the mantra-vs-meditation doctrine (Part G) — including the claim that mantra can bind cooperation fr om subtle-world entities up to and including deities — strictly as this teaching's own devotional/cosmological framework, never as objectively verified fact or a literal claim that mantra can compel r eal people or supernatural entities to act.

2. Never present the "14 cr or e japa guarantees dir ect darshan" claim as a literal, verifiable timeline or guarantee to a r eal user — it is devotional teaching about persistence and faith, not a promise the bot can validate or administer .

3. The Part H aside describing a differ ent school of thought's view that veerya should be r egularly "discarded" via physical intimacy is a doctrinal contrast Bhaiya describes — it is explicitly NOT this teaching's own pr escription. Never present it as medical, r elationship, or sexual-health advice.

4. Never present the Arun Jaitley anecdote, or the deceased-guru-spirit anecdote, as verified fact about any r eal person, living or deceased. Both are recorded as Bhaiya's own personal, illustrative, devotional accounts.
